scenes.tts: Every fall, many monarch butterflies fly south through Virginia. Every spring, cherry trees in Washington, D C, burst into bloom. A butterfly has no calendar. A tree has no eyes. So how do plants and animals know when to sleep, bloom, or fly south?

scenes.visual: Monarch and cherry tree blocks with a crossed-out calendar, then the question.
scenes.narration: Every fall, many monarch butterflies fly south through Virginia. Every spring, cherry trees in Washington, D.C., burst into bloom. A butterfly has no calendar. A tree has no eyes. So how do plants and animals know when to sleep, bloom, or fly south?

scenes.tts: Start with one day. A circadian rhythm is a pattern that repeats about every twenty-four hours. Light and darkness help keep it in step with the day. Many owls hunt at night and rest in the day. Tree squirrels do the opposite. In many animals, the rhythm keeps going for a while in steady darkness. So part of the timing comes from inside the body.

scenes.tts: Plants respond too, often by growing. A tropism is plant growth toward or away from something. Light shines from one side. Cells on the shaded side of the stem grow longer than cells on the lit side. The longer side pushes the stem into a bend toward the light.
scenes.visual: Seedling stem of cell blocks, light from the right; shaded-side cells lengthen and the stem bends toward the light.

scenes.tts: Now think about a Virginia winter. Days are short, nights are cold, and many foods are hard to find. Cues like day length and temperature help time the responses. Monarchs migrate south in fall. Migration is the seasonal movement of animals from one region to another and back. Dormancy is a resting state. Growth slows or stops, but the living thing stays alive. Hibernation is dormancy in animals. A groundhog's body temperature drops, so it uses less stored fat.

scenes.tts: Are these behaviors learned? For monarchs, mostly not. An instinct is a behavior an animal inherits and can do without being taught. A monarch flying south has never made the trip before.
scenes.visual: Question, then the word instinct; a young monarch heading south with no guide.
scenes.narration: Are these behaviors learned? For monarchs, mostly not. An instinct is a behavior an animal inherits and can do without being taught. A monarch flying south has never made the trip before.

scenes.tts: So how do they know? They respond to cues, such as light, day length, and temperature. In animals, many of these responses are inherited instincts. Some changes last for many years, like a warming climate. Those can shift when these responses happen.
scenes.visual: Three timescales stacked: each day, each season, many years; cue chips on the left; the last row shows timing able to shift.
